finding: Targeted bank refinement does not resolve the G2 discrepancy. At bank targets 0.05 m and 0.025 m, G2 level RMSE is 0.05566 and 0.05528 m, versus 0.05552 m on the corrected original mesh; speed RMSE is 0.8368 and 0.8431 m/s, versus 0.8385 m/s. At 20 s the fitted depth-gradient front lies at x = 2.913 and 2.894 m, versus 2.862 m on the original mesh, while G2 is at x = 2.650 m. All three sampled fronts separate supercritical from subcritical normal flow, but G2 remains upstream of the deeper, slower state. The earlier broad refinement moves the fitted front farther downstream to x = 3.162 m. These meshes do not demonstrate convergence.
momentum: The original-mesh corrected solution has no unaccounted momentum term at the precision of this audit. In the G2 control volume, mean x-force per density over 15–25 s is +0.02305 m⁴/s² from numerical face flux, −0.01357 m⁴/s² from reflective-wall reaction and −0.01537 m⁴/s² from Manning friction, producing the computed momentum rate of −0.00589 m⁴/s². Both wet/dry momentum-reset terms are exactly zero in that region. The closure check verifies the accounting; it does not prove that the represented geometry, force laws or resulting jump location reproduce the laboratory experiment.
next: Further bank refinement or tuning wall drag is not supported as a demonstrated remedy by these results. The next priority is a source-led reconciliation of the physical geometry and observation coordinates: throat shape/width, obstruction footprint/orientation, gauge positions and gate-release history. The earlier drawing-versus-DEM differences should be resolved from authoritative records rather than fitted to G2. Independently review the recovered measurement markers and obtain the original series if available. Then qualify a short, controlled geometry or release variant only when that evidence identifies a specific change. Retain FLAT/MEAN as the working control; consider a new flux or sub-cell treatment only with an independent test that isolates its deficiency.
